findings.text: Cgroup aware writeback lookup exposes the inode associated writeback object, while the control sensitive form prefers an already attached writeback when available and otherwise uses the filesystem default.
Without cgroup writeback, inode association always means the device default, control information is ignored, creation for current context yields the same default, and the enabled test never succeeds.
When cgroup writeback is compiled out, the unlocked observation region collapses to a direct lookup with an empty closer, and memory and block offline notifications have no effect.

When cgroup writeback tracking is active for a filesystem, querying the association expects one of the inode, page cache or writeback list protections to be held, while the unlocked variant internally substitutes read side protection with conditional page cache exclusion during ownership switches.
Boot time reservation interface for a named contiguous area, delegating placement to the node aware declaration with no node affinity.
Contiguous management limits state that the area count follows kernel configuration, the name capacity is sixty four, and the minimum alignment scales from pageblock granularity to bytes.

Compaction urgency distinguishes full synchronous, light synchronous and asynchronous modes, where full synchronous is the minimum, light synchronous serves as both the costly minimum and the default, and asynchronous is the initial choice.

Compaction outcome vocabulary separates early skips and deferrals, internal signals to try another block, zone wide completion versus partial progress, premature stop on contention, and successful termination that should satisfy the allocation.
The free gap needed for a given order grows exponentially with order but is capped by the cluster maximum, ensuring the free scanner can accommodate a split while migration isolates stay bounded.
Exposes whether the calling context is the background compaction thread by testing a dedicated thread flag.

When compaction support is absent, suitability always reports false, isolation reset and background thread control and wakeup do nothing, and node registration reports success with an empty unregister.

Without coherent pool support, pool creation always fails, destruction and freeing are empty, allocation always fails, managed creation also fails with empty destroy, the generic creation forwards to the node form with no affinity, and zeroing allocation requests zero filled memory from the same path.

Allocation mode queries distinguish blocking versus spinning versus reclaim capabilities, exact flag containment, combined input filesystem availability, and whether compaction is permitted by configuration and input allowance.
A helper supplies the conventional kernel allocation mode as the default when callers provide no explicit mode.

Optional zone selectors collapse to normal when the corresponding constrained zone is unavailable, and the width used to encode zones in the table is two in the compact case versus the architecture zone shift otherwise.

Zone choice derives from a packed table indexed by the zone relevant flag bits, mapping plain and movable combinations to normal, device, high memory or movable zones, with a separate mask marking architecturally impossible flag mixes as erroneous.

Node fallback policy selects a no fallback list only for strict local requests under NUMA and otherwise allows fallback, with per node lists offset by that policy and node data access differing between single node and multi node builds, while online status reflects the online state.
Nested allocation derives a restricted mode that preserves the caller blocking personality and lockdep opt out while forcing no retry, no memalloc and no warn behavior.
Bulk acquisition helpers provide transparent wrappers around a node specific core, defaulting an unspecified node to the current memory node.
Strict local allocations that suppress warnings still emit a diagnostic with stack trace when targeting an offline node, otherwise remaining silent.

Page and folio acquisition forms centralize on node specific folio allocation for the current node, with policy and area sensitive forms collapsing to the same path in these fragments and single page helpers extracting the head page, including a lock free path.
Exact size, raw address and zeroed page helpers expose order zero shortcuts and device constrained variants as thin wrappers over the generic page acquisition and release primitives.
Architecture hooks for page acquisition and release are defined as empty placeholders, allowing platforms to interpose without affecting generic callers.
Contiguous request attributes form a distinct bitwise integer type, separating ordinary requests from management requests at the type level.
Ordinary contiguous request attributes have a zero value, while the management request value occupies the lowest bit.
Contiguous range and page acquisition interfaces for frozen and ordinary cases are exposed as transparent wrappers that preserve caller arguments.

Raw allocation flag bits assign distinct positions to placement, reclaimability, high access, input output, zeroing, direct and background reclaim, write intent, warning suppression, retry and failure handling, memory reserve access, compound pages, node restriction, accounting and tagging, with unused and conditional positions for skip handling and lockdep opt out.

Typed allocation flags mirror the raw bits with strong typing, including a combined zone mask, a combined reclaim mask, and shift and mask values derived from the final bit position for validating mode width.
Header inclusion guards use distinct macros to ensure single inclusion of contiguous, compaction, pool and allocation flag interfaces.
The unlock observation cookie carries a switching indicator and saved interrupt state, used to determine whether page cache exclusion must be released when the region closes.
An invalid combination of zone related flags triggers a debug trap during zone resolution, indicating a caller error rather than a runtime fallback.
